scope: Maps closed phrases in the model-visible request-bearing fields (objective and question) to requested analysis class and target claim levels. Used only to derive gold for scoring; never scored as model reasoning and never used as a runtime planner.
match: case-insensitive substring of each request-bearing field; a phrase may occur at most once per field

composition.claims: union of target levels contributed by all rules matched in all request-bearing fields, per axis
composition.analysis_class: the single contributed class; NONE when a composite marker matches, more than one class is contributed, or more than one target level is requested on one axis
composition.unmatched: derivation fails closed; no gold exists

rules.justification: An absolute longitudinal change between two observations is the RES-69 absolute-change estimand; describing it requests the numerical change and a descriptive-change relationship, nothing higher.
A descriptive change explicitly requests the RES-70 DESCRIPTIVE_CHANGE relationship level over a numerical change.
A causal effect on a measured outcome attributes a numerical change between the supplied observations to a cause; the relationship target is RES-70 CAUSAL_EVIDENCE.
Inferring random measurement error requests a reliability estimate of the measurement process, not a claim about change or about a relationship between observations.
A within-athlete association is the RES-70 WITHIN_ATHLETE_ASSOCIATION analysis and requests the ASSOCIATION relationship level only.

rules.phrase: practical or decision meaningfulness of the jump-height change
rules.justification: Judging whether the change between the supplied observations matters for a decision requests the RES-70 PRACTICAL_OR_DECISION_MEANINGFULNESS measurement level about that absolute change.

rules.phrase: large enough to justify a readiness or training decision
rules.justification: Asking whether a change is large enough to justify a readiness or training decision requests the RES-70 PRACTICAL_OR_DECISION_MEANINGFULNESS level; it names no analysis class of its own.
Forcing distinct claims into one estimand has no single registered analysis class.

fields.precedence: objective and question are both user requests. A question identical to the objective (after case and whitespace normalization) is not counted twice. Otherwise rules matched in either field are combined, and the composition rules adjudicate conflicts: a question that adds a distinct claim makes the request composite.
fields.analysis_source: objective must match at least one non-composite rule
fields.unadjudicated_claim_content: a field containing a claim trigger outside every matched phrase fails closed; no gold exists
